title: Grateful Dead Live at Mammoth Gardens on 1970-04-24
lineage: AUD master C-120 > reel 3.75ips > DAT > CD

ai_review.summary: A rough audience recording that’s listenable, featuring a legendary Eleven and a soaring Dark Star from the spring‑70 Mammoth Gardens show.
ai_review.review: The performance is widely praised – the Elevent is described as “one of its best versions,” Dark Star and St. Stephen flow into an unforgettable jam, and even the sleepy first set has moments like a soulful Slow Rider. The audio is an audience mic capture that suffers from mud‑dy highs and occasional drop‑outs, but recent clean‑up work makes it tolerable enough to enjoy the historic music.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rave about the musical content (numerous 5‑star comments) while consistently noting poor or fair sound quality; weighted averaging yields a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Muddy, low‑fidelity mic‑in‑the‑air capture with occasional drop‑outs and missing sections (e.g., part of "A Man's World"); a cleaned‑up version improves clarity but the recording remains rough.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Acoustic first set is a bit sleepy and marked by power‑cut interruptions, but the electric second set builds into a historic jam sequence (Dark Star → St. Stephen → The Eleven) that defines the show’s high point.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple reviewers highlight Jerry's soaring licks and perfect tone, especially on The Eleven and Dark Star.
band_member_comments.Bob: Bob is noted for stage banter (the sit‑down/stand‑up chant) rather than playing.
